title.narrative: Emergency WASH response after cyclone Idai

description.narrative: 21.000 Children,women and men (disaggregated by gender, age, disability) provided with access to safe water as per Sphere standard of 15 litres of water per person per day domestic(drinking, cooking and personal hygiene) purposes.21.000 Children,women and men (disaggregated by gender, age, disability) provided with access to adequate sanitation facilities including access to environmentally friendly conditions free from faeces.21.000 Children,women and men (disaggregated by gender, age, disability) provided with access to hygiene education and information pertaining to safe and hygienic behaviour(functional handwashing facilities and soap or an alternative).

Women, men and children affected by Cyclone IDAI disaster have restored access to safe water, appropriate sanitation and hygiene practices to reduce incidence of diarrheal diseases. Distribution of point of use household water treatment chemicals; Rehabilitation water supply networks; Conducting Participatory Health and Hygiene Education (PHHE); Distribution WASH kits; Provision of temporary sanitation facilities; Training of Environmental Health technicians (EHTs), Village Health Workers (VHWs) and Community Health Workers (CHWs).
Women, men and children affected by Cyclone IDAI disaster have restored access to safe water, appropriate sanitation and hygiene practices to reduce incidence of diarrheal diseases.
